title: No musicians in the family; brass bands and parades
summary: No one in his family played. He followed marching brass bands on Sundays; one band played fairs and Chautauquas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I do too. Did anyone in your family play music? Your father or any brothers or anyone?
No, there wasn't anybody in my family that I know of that played music. But I can never know of this. None of my family were out. None of my brothers or sisters.
Can you remember the earliest music that you heard?
That is, around home or was there any bands or parades or anything of that kind that when you were a boy that you can remember?
Well, yes, there were brass bands, you know, as kids usually. I used to follow those brass bands on Sundays. Oh, yeah. In those parades, you know. What kind of bands did they have?
Did they just play marches or did they play sort of jazz?

Well, they just played marches. A straight marches. Yeah. But now there was a band there that used to play Chautauquas and fairs around there. Yeah, they used to play, sometimes play, get in some of those small towns and played dances, you know. But it was a brass band. Yeah. All about, you usually carry about twelve, fifteen pieces. I see.
